issues.legal_issue: Service of a requisition notice on the owners recorded in the statutory land record satisfies the notice requirement when purchasers have not yet been recorded as owners.
material_facts: The purchasers acquired the land but had not had their names entered in the statutory record of rights when the requisition notice was served.
The authorities served notice on the persons recorded as owners.
The purchasers had applied for mutation, but their names were entered in the record only after the land had been acquired.
issues.conclusion: Service on the recorded owners complied with the notice requirement; the authorities were not required to make further inquiries into unrecorded transfers or search registration records for other owners.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 3(2) of the West Bengal Land (Requisition and Acquisition) Act, 1948 and Rule 3 of the applicable Rules, notice must be served on the owner in the prescribed manner. Sections 50 and 51A(9) of the West Bengal Land Reforms Act, 1955 provide for the statutory record of rights and a presumption that its entries are correct until proved otherwise; Section 3 of that Act gives it overriding effect where laws are inconsistent. The Court relied on Sureshchanora C. Mehta v. State of Karnataka and Winky Dilawari v. Amritsar Improvement Trust for the principle that authorities need not conduct a roving inquiry or routinely search registration records to identify persons not shown in the relevant official record.

predicates.requisition_notice_challenge: A proceeding challenges whether notice for a land requisition was properly served.
predicates.purchasers_not_recorded_when_notice_serv: Persons who had purchased the land were not entered as owners in the relevant official land record when notice was served.
predicates.notice_served_on_recorded_owners: The authority served notice on the persons identified as owners in the relevant official land record.
predicates.notice_requirement_satisfied: The notice requirement for the requisition is satisfied.

issues.definition: When a requisition notice is challenged, service on the recorded owners satisfies the notice requirement if purchasers were not yet recorded as owners when the notice was served.

issues.legal_issue: Acquisition of land for a state-controlled housing project that substantially provides affordable homes to the community serves a public purpose even when a joint venture participates and may earn profit.
material_facts: The land was acquired for a housing complex intended to address the shortage of housing.
The project was undertaken through a joint sector company formed with a private company, while the State and Housing Board retained control and guidance over the company and project.
The project planned a substantial proportion of homes for lower- and middle-income groups at controlled prices, with revenue from higher-income homes helping subsidise those homes.
The State and Housing Board set conditions for the use of the land and the housing scheme, including eligibility and allotment arrangements.
issues.conclusion: The housing project served a public purpose, and the acquisition and use of the joint sector company did not amount to a colourable exercise, arbitrariness, irrationality, or abuse of power.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3(1) and Section 4(1a) of the West Bengal Land (Requisition and Acquisition) Act, 1948 permit requisition and acquisition for specified public purposes, including creating better living conditions through housing. Sections 17, 18 and 27A of the West Bengal Housing Board Act support housing schemes and entrusting their execution to a joint sector company. The Court relied on S.M. Nandy v. State of West Bengal in discussing the Act's validity, and on L. Chandra Kumar v. Union of India and Reg. v. Hillingdon L.B.C., Ex p. Puhlhofer for the scope and restraint of judicial review. It also discussed H.D. Vora v. State of Maharashtra on the need for the State to establish a public purpose. The Court held that a profit element does not by itself defeat public purpose where the project is controlled by public authorities and serves community housing needs; courts should not minutely review a policy serving those needs absent grounds such as mala fides, statutory or constitutional conflict, or abuse of power.

rule.if: housing_acquisition_challenge and housing_shortage_addressed and affordable_housing_substantially_provided and public_authority_controls_joint_project

predicates.housing_acquisition_challenge: A proceeding challenges an acquisition made for a housing project.
predicates.housing_shortage_addressed: The project is intended to address a housing need in the community.
predicates.affordable_housing_substantially_provide: The project provides a substantial share of homes on affordable terms for people who otherwise face difficulty obtaining housing.
predicates.public_authority_controls_joint_project: Public authorities retain meaningful control over the joint project and its housing scheme.
predicates.acquisition_serves_public_purpose_and_is: The acquisition serves a public purpose and is not a colourable exercise of power.

issues.definition: An acquisition challenged in connection with a housing project serves a public purpose and is not colourable when it addresses community housing needs, substantially provides affordable homes, and remains under public authority control.
